'''Cornelia Druțu''' is a Romanian mathematician notable for her contributions in the area of [[geometric group theory]].<ref name="CDHP">{{cite web|url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/drutu/|title=Cornelia Druţu's Homepage|author=Cornelia Druțu}}</ref> She is Professor of mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name="CDHP"/> and Fellow<ref name="exeter">
{{cite web|url=https://www.exeter.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-cornelia-drutu/|title=Professor Cornelia Druțu|author=Exeter College, Oxford|author-link=Exeter College, Oxford}}</ref> of [[Exeter College, Oxford]].

== Education and career ==
Druțu was born in [[Iași]], Romania. She attended the [[Emil Racoviță]] High School (now the National College Emil Racoviță<ref name="CNER">{{cite web|url=https://racovita.ro|title=The National College ''Emil Racoviță''}}</ref>) in Iași. She earned a [[B.S.]] in Mathematics from the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]], where besides attending the core courses she received extra curricular teaching in [[geometry]] and [[topology]] from Professor Liliana Răileanu.<ref name="exeter"/>

In 1996 Druțu earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Mathematics from [[University of Paris-Sud]], with a thesis entitled ''Réseaux non uniformes des groupes de Lie semi-simple de rang supérieur et invariants de quasiisométrie'', written under the supervision of [[Pierre Pansu]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=53429|name=Cornelia Druțu}}</ref> She then joined the [[Lille University of Science and Technology|University of Lille 1]] as Maître de conférences (MCF). In 2004 she earned her [[Habilitation]] degree from the University of Lille 1.<ref name="Hab">{{cite web|url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/drutu/thesehdr.ps|title=Habilitation Cornelia Druțu|author=Cornelia Druțu}}</ref>

In 2009 she became Professor of mathematics at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]].<ref name="CDHP"/>

She held visiting positions at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in [[Bonn]], the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] in [[Bures-sur-Yvette]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]]. She visited the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] in [[Cambridge]] as holder of a Simons Fellowship.<ref name="SF">{{cite web|url=http://www.newton.ac.uk/about/fellowships/simons/|title=Simons Visiting Fellowships|access-date=2019-01-05|archive-date=2019-01-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190106010650/http://www.newton.ac.uk/about/fellowships/simons/}}</ref> From 2013 to 2020 she chaired the [[European Mathematical Society]]/European Women in Mathematics scientific panel of women mathematicians.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-17 |title=EMS/EWM Scientific Panel |url=https://womenandmath.wordpress.com/emsewm-scientific-committee/ |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=Women and Mathematics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Caroline |first=Series |date=October 2013 |title=European Level Organisations for Women Mathematicians |url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/european_level_organisationseuroversion2013.pdf |website=European Women in Mathematics}}</ref>

== Awards ==

In 2009, Druțu was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]] for her work in geometric group theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations09.html|title=Prize Winners 2009|author=London Mathematical Society|access-date=2010-10-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091023171104/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations09.html|archive-date=2009-10-23}}</ref>

In 2017, Druțu was awarded a Simons Visiting Fellowship.<ref name="SF"/>

== Publications ==

===Selected contributions===

* The [[quasi-isometry]] invariance of relative hyperbolicity; a characterization of [[relatively hyperbolic group]]s using geodesic triangles, similar to the one of [[hyperbolic group]]s.
* A classification of relatively hyperbolic groups up to quasi-isometry; the fact that a group with a quasi-isometric embedding in a relatively hyperbolic metric space, with image at infinite distance from any peripheral set, must be relatively hyperbolic.
* The non-distortion of [[horosphere]]s in [[symmetric space]]s of non-compact type and in Euclidean [[Building (mathematics)|building]]s, with constants depending only on the [[Weyl group]].
* The quadratic filling for certain [[Linear group|linear]] [[solvable group]]s (with uniform constants for large classes of such groups).
* A construction of a 2-generated recursively presented group with continuum many non-[[homeomorphic]] [[asymptotic cone]]s. Under the [[continuum hypothesis]], a [[finitely generated group]] may have at most continuum many non-homeomorphic asymptotic cones, hence the result is sharp.
* A characterization of [[Kazhdan's property (T)]] and of the [[Haagerup property]] using affine isometric actions on [[median space]]s.
* A study of generalizations of Kazhdan's property (T) for [[Uniformly convex space|uniformly convex]] [[Banach space]]s.
* A proof that [[random group]]s satisfy strengthened versions of Kazhdan's property (T) for high enough density; a proof that for random groups the [[conformal dimension]] of the boundary is connected to the maximal value of ''p'' for which the groups have fixed point properties for isometric affine actions on [[Lp space|<math>L^p</math> space]]s.
